That is a tough one. I always have a hard time assembling a favourites list for any genre. There are just so many movies that I enjoy for differing reasons. And my favourites aren't set in stone, of course. There are always more movies to watch.

But if I had to pick, or die, it would probably be these:

  1. Alien (1979)
  2. The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974)
  3. The Thing (1982)
  4. The Evil Dead (1981)
  5. A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984)

A Nightmare on Elm Street probably shouldn't/wouldn't be up there (It's not really a great film - though parts of it are), except that it's one of the first films that I can recall scaring the crap out of me, which I think planted the seed of my love for horror (and in particular the slasher subgenre). I rented and watched it when I was a kid (sometime in the early 90s), and subsequently rented the rest of the sequels, and then anything else with a cover that caught my eye (I discovered Friday the 13th and it's sequels not too long after, and then Halloween and it's sequels). I am glad my parents let me rent horror movies when I was younger. Some may call it slightly negligent, but I think that's bullshit. I turned out alright (I'm pretty sure any issues that I may, or may not have, have nothing to do with watching horror movies as a kid). Now I just thoroughly enjoy horror flicks.

Halloween (1978) could be an alternate fifth position. John Carpenter is probably one of my favourite directors ever.
